channel.title: The Wealth Whisperer: A CPWA Casebook
channel.description: A private, drama-filled study companion made for Fabi on her way to the CPWA. Each episode follows the Chicago Booth CPWA course order and turns the material into cases with a recurring cast of clients, heirs, in-laws and advisors, with a pop quiz and a Director's call at the end.

item.title: Episode 2: Behavioral Finance & Investor Psychology (Part 1)
item.itunes:title: Episode 2: Behavioral Finance & Investor Psychology (Part 1)
item.description:
Section 2: Behavioral Finance & Investor Psychology, Part 1. This section is 6% of the CPWA exam, within Human Dynamics (18%). This is the first episode in the new format: US-only material, a structured review of every learning objective, and one short domestic case.
Covered: the biology of financial decisions (System 1 and System 2, amygdala, nucleus accumbens, insula, prefrontal cortex); expected value theory; expected utility, including normative, descriptive and prescriptive views, the shape of the utility curve, certainty equivalent and risk premium; Markowitz's mean-variance model and the efficient frontier; prospect theory (reference points, loss aversion, the S-shaped value function, probability weighting, the disposition effect); Andrew Lo's adaptive markets hypothesis; how the theories compare and how behavioral finance evolved; and cognitive biases, both belief-perseverance and information-processing, including anchoring and adjustment, availability, framing, outcome and recency.
The short case is The Case of the Miami Beach Pitch. It's followed by Teo's Pop Quiz (six exam-style questions) and a Lightning Recap with Doña Pilar.
Coming in Part 2: emotional biases, the four behavioral investor types, accommodate vs. educate, and generational differences.
All characters and firms are fictional.

item.title: Episode 1: Ethics (The Pilot)
item.itunes:title: Episode 1: Ethics (The Pilot)
item.description:
Module: Overview & Ethics. Three case files and one question that sounds simple and never is: who, exactly, is my client?
The Case of the Three Wedding Rings: Don Octavio, a US citizen who died in Colombia, a widow without a US passport, and a lawyer who arrives much too early with papers to sign. Covers worldwide estate tax, the QDOT and conflicts of interest. The Case of the Silent Trust: the Castañedas, a Delaware dynasty trust, and a son who starts asking questions. Covers confidentiality and preparing heirs. The Case of the Sixty-Thousand-Dollar Teacup: tea with Doña Pilar and US estate tax for nonresident non-citizens.
The IWI Code of Professional Responsibility runs through all three, followed by Teo's Pop Quiz, Fabi's Call and a Lightning Recap with Doña Pilar.
All characters, families, firms and banks are fictional.

item.title: Episode 0: Introduction & Meet the Cast
item.itunes:title: Episode 0: Introduction & Meet the Cast
item.description:
Welcome to the Casebook, Fabi. Meet your host Margo (a senior wealth strategist, CPWA and part-time detective) and Teo (a junior associate, quiz master and proud owner of a buzzer), and find out how every episode works: Cold Open, the Huddle, the Case Room, the Real-World File, Teo's Pop Quiz, Fabi's Call and the Lightning Recap. The whole thing fits your commute.
Then meet the recurring cast you'll follow through the course: Don Octavio Salcedo and his box of home videos ("the Octavio Archive"), the widow Valentina, the young heiress Sofía, Rodrigo the in-law with a crypto hotel in Tulum, the family lawyer Dr. Villalba, the Castañedas of Guatemala City, the Montalvos of Lima, Preston Hale the private banker, Kendra from Growth, and Doña Pilar, who will ask the same question five times (on purpose).
All characters, families, firms and banks are fictional.
